Version 1.0.2 of smyx-pet-carrier-respiratory-rate-analysis introduces significant changes to user identity handling and documentation:

- Removed all user-facing open-id requirements; identity management is now handled automatically by the system without user intervention.
- Updated the SKILL.md to clarify that users should not be prompted for or exposed to any internal identity values.
- Revised workflow documentation to reflect stricter privacy and simplified user interactions—users now only need to upload videos or request reports.
- Maintained strict requirements that historical report queries must always use cloud APIs; local or memory-based report queries remain prohibited.
- Cleaned up redundant documentation and removed files no longer relevant to the new workflow.

- Updated open-id (api-key) configuration path: now checks scripts/config.yaml in the skill root directory instead of skills/smyx_common/scripts/config.yaml.
- License information added to SKILL.md (MIT-0).
- Removed deprecated file skill-card.md.
- Adjusted documentation instructions and workflows in SKILL.md to match new config structure and file paths.
- No changes to core logic or API usage; existing analysis and reporting features are unchanged.

Initial release of smyx-pet-carrier-respiratory-rate-analysis.

- Enables automated respiratory rate analysis for pets inside airline carriers/crates using uploaded videos or URLs.
- Detects chest/abdomen rise-fall cycles to calculate resting breathing frequency (breaths/min).
- Triggers alerts when respiratory rate exceeds the safety threshold (>40 bpm) to help identify hypoxia, anxiety, or abnormal health events during air transport.
- Includes strict open-id retrieval processes to manage user history and access.
- Provides standardized report outputs, historical report listing in Markdown tables with direct links, and multi-language support (English/Chinese).
- Designed for use in pet airline carriers, cargo, and long-distance transport scenarios.
